finding.name: ACTIVE_TURN_COMPOSITE_IDENTITY_NOT_ENFORCED_BY_INDEPENDENT_FOREIGN_KEYS
finding.mechanism: An active_turns row can be individually foreign-key valid while its referenced turn or workspace episode belongs to another canonical session/user perspective.
finding.risk: The canonical retrieval entry identity can become semantically forked across Gabriel/Andreas despite all individual SQLite foreign keys resolving.

contracts: active user equals session user and turn user
turn session equals requested active session
workspace episode session equals requested active session

isolated_mechanism_regression.setup: Minimal SQLite schema preserving the relevant sessions/turns/workspace_episodes/active_turns foreign-key topology; non-target module imports stubbed only so the exact retrieval.py blob can load.

corrupt_case.description: Gabriel active turn references an Andreas workspace episode whose observation_turn_id is Gabriel's turn; every individual FK resolves.

coherent_case.description: Gabriel active turn, turn and workspace episode all bind to the same Gabriel session and observation turn.

isolated_mechanism_regression.limitations: Not a full private-repository checkout, not the full pytest suite, not OCI build/start, not Clerk/browser/PTY/Claude acceptance.

next_exact_step: Run the rebased PR's exact full-source retrieval/lifecycle regression set in an admitted isolated runner; if green and ancestry remains clean, merge the identity fence without importing the divergent Stage-B stack.
